title: Azure Storage Overview
description: Understand Azure Storage accounts, redundancy options, and the four main storage services.

data.text: Azure Storage is a set of managed services for files, messages, tables, and disks. For ASP.NET Core apps, the most important services are Blob, Queue, and File storage.
A storage account is the top-level object. It provides a unique namespace, access keys, and redundancy settings for all contained services.

rows: Zone redundant across datacenters in one region
Geo-redundant with read access to secondary region

data.title: Services used in this course
items: **Blob Storage** — object storage for files, images, and backups
**Queue Storage** — simple message queues for decoupled work
**File Storage** — SMB file shares for legacy or shared access needs
**Table Storage** — schemaless NoSQL key-value data, covered later in a separate module

data.title: Prefer Blob over File
data.text: For new ASP.NET Core apps, Blob Storage is usually the better choice over File Storage because it is cheaper, more scalable, and easier to consume from C#.

data.title: Create a storage account with Azure CLI
data.content: Use the `az storage account create` command to create the infrastructure.
data.code:
az storage account create \
  --name demostorageaccount \
  --resource-group azure-for-aspnet-rg \
  --location eastus \
  --sku Standard_LRS \
  --kind StorageV2

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: A storage account groups blob, queue, file, and table services
Choose redundancy based on durability and budget
Blob Storage is the default choice for files in new apps
Queue Storage is the simplest way to add background processing
data.takeaway: Start with one storage account in the same region as your App Service plan to keep data transfer costs low.
